items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: You take this fella, like Hickman... And we was playing next door to one another.

ctx.x: You see, that time when I come up, during my time coming up, you couldn't get in the band if you couldn't read.

You know, that's what I said. Well, that's why they hired me at the Japanese T-Guard. Because I was just not clear. I'd hold a note, see, when they finished playing, I'd hold a note. Do it, then it's not the right key, you know. Couldn't make no jazz. I didn't know if I could read that. Yeah. That's right. But I tell you, in them days, it helped so much. Now you take this fella, like Hickman, he could play a little saxophone, but he couldn't read so much, you see. And we was playing next door to one another. And…

Hold that door on the air. Always could read. That's all he could do, read. That fellow, boy, that fellow. Always could read. You buy that piece of music, that was it. That was it. Always could read. In the never band, you played baritone.
